single_hypothesis: Replacing the backward TQue machinery with raw double-buffered input and explicit MTE2_V/V_MTE2/V_MTE3/MTE3_V events removes queue bookkeeping from the backward hot path (main attack on point 5) while leaving every forward byte untouched.
changed_mechanism: backward input: TQue<VECIN, depth 2> -> raw TBuf backwardBuf_ with 2 manually ping-ponged slots (same 4N bytes, same allocation order)
backward output: TQue<VECOUT, depth 1> -> raw TBuf outBuf_ (2N bytes)

explicit events reproducing TQue semantics exactly: MTE2_V issued after each DataCopy (=EnQue), waited before each Cast/Axpy (=DeQue); V_MTE2 set after PipeBarrier post-compute (=FreeTensor), waited before slot overwrite (=AllocTensor); V_MTE3 set/wait around the output cast (=VECOUT EnQue/DeQue); MTE3_V waited before the next task's cast and set after CopyRowsOut (=AllocTensor/FreeTensor); one final MTE3_V drain before kernel exit
replica-0 read is issued at task start; replica k+1 is prefetched into the other slot before computing replica k, preserving the TQue version's overlap
unchanged_mechanisms: entire forward path (single-pass + ping-pong + events) - verified byte-identical objects for keys 1/27
E2 FP16 backward Axpy / BF16 Cast+Add arithmetic and replica order
all DMA calls and parameters, padding, offsets
host tiling and the 4-kernel direction-specialized tiling key

event_dependency_audit.MTE2_V mte2ToV[slot]: RAW: MTE2 wrote the slot -> Vector Cast/Axpy may read
event_dependency_audit.V_MTE2 vToMte2[slot]: WAR: Vector finished reading the slot (guarded by PipeBarrier) -> next MTE2 may overwrite; pre-set for both slots at kernel start
event_dependency_audit.V_MTE3 vToMte3: RAW: final CastFromFloat done -> MTE3 CopyRowsOut may read
event_dependency_audit.MTE3_V mte3ToV: WAR: MTE3 finished reading outLocal -> next task's CastFromFloat may overwrite; pre-set at start, drained at kernel end

validation.actual_kernel: 5 CA-simulator cases executed cleanly (no deadlock, no tiling/load errors): fp16/bf16 backward small, fp16 backward m8, fp16/bf16 forward small

simulator.interpretation: Largest single-mechanism instruction reduction so far: backward -27.5% (small) and -33.8% (m=8), scalar -142/-412 calls respectively; forward exactly unchanged. Expect the platform effect to concentrate on scalar-bound point 5 and (overlapped, smaller) on any backward mid/large points.

platform.model_check: model predicts 74.96 from displayed times, observed 75.16 (0.2 gap, rounding)

e6_note: m-loop template unrolling (16 objects) was evaluated and skipped: per-task saving ~3(m-1) instructions is far below E5's signal and below the noise floor; not worth the object explosion. FP16-backward valueFp32Buf skip deliberately NOT included to avoid repeating E3's unattributed mid-point regression (UB layout shift remains a suspect).
limitations: Single platform observation will be within/near the +-1.2 noise band unless the queue bookkeeping cost is larger on real hardware than in simulation
No actual-kernel golden comparison outside CANNJudge; correctness rests on event-semantics equivalence with TQue plus clean simulator execution
key_learning: Point 5 stayed at 3.86 us (band 3.68-3.88) despite -27.5% backward instructions: points 1/5 are NOT scalar-bound; remaining ~2.3 us gap lives in launch + DMA latency chain + end sync. Scalar-side optimization on small points has reached its floor. Next real upside: mid points 2/4 via host-side task/core load balance.
